text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- U.S.: No deadlines in Hebron pact. United States will help Israel capitalise on agreement.
- Strike off today after mass shutdown.
- Palestinian killed in Gush Katif.
- Woman, 52, gives birth to triplets.
- Defeat of tax-credit cut for married women.
- 1996 growth slowed to 4.4 percent, unemployment down to 6.5 percent.
- Cement firms: No room here for Japanese producer.
- Bankers: Strike's month's-end timing may be harmful.
- Communications Minister to Bezeq Communications: Stop favouring own Internet service.
GLOBES
- Serious slowdown in public sector. Employers: We'll stop the transfer of organisation tax.
- Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu: Investers who see wild strikes -- could depart.
- Slowdown in pace of economic growth in 1996.
- Omani foreign minister: Gulf states to consider reimposing indirect boycott on Israel.
MAARIV
- "Opposition front" to Hebron deal grows.
- Television license fee to be 447 shekels in 1997.
- Summary of 1996: Serious slowdown in growth, export -- and a crisis in real estate.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Revolt in the coalition. Netanyahu is furious: Government suffers two blows in Knesset in a single day.
- Tomorrow: The start of morning broadcasts on Israel's Channel Two.
- Yedioth Ahronoth poll: 58 percent of the public don't know the reason for the strike.
- Israel Aircraft Industries in contacts on participation in satellite company of Lockheed-Martin and Mitsubishi.
HAARETZ
- Netanyahu promises to bring Hebron agreement to Knesset for approval; At least six ministers oppose the accord.
- Histadrut settling for strike only at seaports today.
- Tel Aviv Stock Exchange -- a third disappointing year.
- Strike damage since last Thursday estimated at 100 million shekels.
